title: Base change of a zero-dimensional scheme to a bigger field
statement:
Let $k\subseteq k'$ be a field extension with $k$ algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $C$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with $\dim C\le0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $C_{k'}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ be the base change with projection $\pi:C_{k'}\to C$ [def-pc-base-change]. Then:
1. $|C|$ is a finite discrete space, every $c\in|C|$ is a closed point with residue field $\kappa(c)=k$ [def-weil-residue-field].
2. $C_{k'}$ has dimension $\le0$, and $\pi$ induces a bijection (indeed a homeomorphism of finite discrete spaces) $|C_{k'}|\to|C|$: the fibre $\pi^{-1}(c)$ is the one point of $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(c)\otimes_kk')=\operatorname{Spec}k'$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00KH (Noetherian of dimension 0 = Artinian, finitely many maximal primes), Lemma Tag 00P4 (lemma-dimension-at-a-point-preserved-field-extension: dimension at a point is preserved by ground field extension); residue fields by the Nullstellensatz (Tag 00FV); fibres of a base change: literature/stacks-project/schemes.tex Lemma Tag 01JT (points of a fibre product)

proof.text: *Clause (1): $|C|$ is finite and discrete.* By the conventions [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and of finite type (locally of finite type and quasi-compact), and $\dim C\le0$ by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-dim-zero-artinian] (finite type over a field gives Noetherian affine pieces; a Noetherian ring of dimension $0$ is Artinian, Stacks 00KH), $C$ is locally Artinian, its underlying space $|C|$ is discrete and finite, and every point $c\in|C|$ is closed [def-weil-closed-points] (in a discrete space every singleton is closed). If $C=\emptyset$ all assertions below are vacuous.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00KH (lemma-Noetherian-dimension-0) and its proof (the spectrum of a Noetherian ring of dimension 0 is a finite discrete space)

proof.text: *Clause (1): $\kappa(c)=k$.* Let $c\in|C|$. By step 1, $c$ is a closed point of $C$, and $C$ is locally of finite type over the algebraically closed field $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] (Nullstellensatz, Stacks 00FV: $\kappa(c)$ is a finite extension of $k$, hence equal to $k$ as $k$ is algebraically closed), the map $k\to\kappa(c)$ induced by the structure morphism on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism.

source.place: Theorem Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz), applied to an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A\ni c$ with $A$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra and the maximal ideal of $c$

proof.text: *Clause (2): the fibres of $\pi$.* Write $C_{k'}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ with projections $\pi:C_{k'}\to C$ and $\mathrm{pr}:C_{k'}\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ [def-pc-base-change]. The spectrum of a field has exactly one point (its zero ideal) [def-weil-affine-spectrum]: let $s$ be the point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\eta$ that of $\operatorname{Spec}k'$, with $\kappa(s)=k$ and $\kappa(\eta)=k'$ [def-weil-residue-field]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] (Stacks 01JT), the points of $C_{k'}$ correspond bijectively to quadruples $(c,y,t,\mathfrak p)$ with $c\in C$, $y\in\operatorname{Spec}k'$, $t\in\operatorname{Spec}k$ having the same image, and $\mathfrak p$ a prime of $\kappa(c)\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(y)$, the point lying over $c$ under $\pi$. Necessarily $y=\eta$ and $t=s$, so $\pi^{-1}(c)$ is in bijection with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(c)\otimes_kk')$. By step 2 the structure map $k\to\kappa(c)$ is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras, so $\kappa(c)\otimes_kk'\cong k\otimes_kk'\cong k'$ (the map $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$), a field; its spectrum has exactly one point. Hence $\pi^{-1}(c)$ is a single point for every $c\in|C|$, i.e. $\pi:|C_{k'}|\to|C|$ is a bijection; in particular $|C_{k'}|$ is finite (step 1).

*Clause (2): $\dim C_{k'}\le0$ and $\pi$ is a homeomorphism.* By step 1, $C$ is (locally) of finite type over $k$ with discrete underlying space. By [lem-weil-pbc-discrete-field-base-change-artinian] (Stacks 00P4 in dimension $0$), $C_{k'}$ is locally Artinian, its underlying space is discrete and $\dim C_{k'}\le0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. So $\pi:|C_{k'}|\to|C|$ is a continuous bijection (step 3) between finite discrete spaces; its inverse is continuous because every map out of a discrete space is, so $\pi$ is a homeomorphism of finite discrete spaces.
